script.base: Market prices a close KC home lead, not a blowout: implied KC 27.0 / IND 23.5 on a 50.5 total, so both offenses should get volume. Base flow is competitive into the fourth quarter with KC ahead by a score late, Hunt carrying the late clock as the only healthy early-down back, and Mahomes still throwing enough (Kelce/Rice) to hit a 27-point team total. IND's last three listed games are weeks 8-9-10 and KC's are 8-9-11, so this read treats IND as coming off a week-11 bye and KC as off a week-10 bye then a week-11 game; pace itself is not in the pack.
script.flip1: KC scores early, the 37% blitz suppresses IND (EPA/dropback 0.06 vs blitz vs 0.22 clean), and the margin stretches past one score. Taylor's rush volume dies as IND throws (Pierce/Pittman/Warren), Hunt's carries rise further, and KC skill-player late snaps are the blowout risk.
script.flip2: Taylor controls the clock, IND leads or ties, and KC abandons the run. Hunt's carry line dies; Mahomes airs it out to Kelce and Rice (Worthy only if active), so KC pass overs and the Hunt rush over need opposite scripts.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Hunt: IND led from the second quarter, KC threw, Suamataia was inactive, and Smith mixed in enough that Hunt finished around 8 carries and under 34.5, a rerun of the 18-yard game rather than the 40-59 cluster. Kelce: Worthy played a full snap count, IND sat in a shell that took away the middle, and Kelce finished in the mid-40s to mid-50s while Rice or Brown took the intermediate work, with the late KC lead spent on Hunt runs. That counter is real but not stronger than the read — Pacheco is already Out and Hunt's line is far under a 49-yard recent role, and Kelce's target share plus a missing LB still beats a 61.5 number unless the bracket actually happens. Taylor over 98.5 was considered and dropped in the pre-mortem: 7.62 YPC will not repeat against 4.34 YPC allowed, the dog script can kill carries, and last4 already has a 45. Pierce over 68.5 was dropped because the 37% blitz / 0.06 EPA split is a stronger kill case than the 4-for-4 form is a reason to force a third leg.
slip_story: One story only: KC moderate favorite in a high-total, still-competitive game. Stack Hunt rush yards over 34.5 (lead back, Pacheco out, late carries if KC leads) with Kelce receiving yards over 61.5 (primary target, Carlies out, total keeps the passing game alive). They win together if KC scores around its 27 implied points without a blowout or a full abandon-the-run. Do not add Taylor rush over, a game under, or Pierce deep over — those need the IND clock-control script, a weather slog we cannot see, or explosives through a heavy blitz. Two legs, no touchdowns, one market per player. Not placed.
